newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile court grants Chilectra power order.
newsitem.headline: Chile court grants Chilectra power order.

text.p: A Chilean appeal court has granted an order sought by power firm Chilectra to stop the government from fixing new distribution tariffs which are expected to be sharply below current levels, said Chilectra.
Chilectra said the order will stop the National Energy Commission from setting the new prices which will be in force for four years from November.
"The injunction stops the tariff process until the aspects which have been questioned by Chilectra have been resolved," said the statement.
Chilectra, Chile's largest power distributor, has complained that commission's procedure for setting the tariffs is "illegal and arbitary."
Although the board has not published any details of the new prices, tariffs are expected to be cut by up to 10 percent, say analysts.
Commission officials said, however, that the court order will not stop them from continuing the process of setting distribution prices.
"Although the appeal has been accepted, the injunction does alter the process of setting the tariffs," said president Alejandro Jadresic.
Chilectra's sister company generator Endesa said Monday that it will appeal the commission's plans to slash generating prices by 11.3 percent in real terms.
Power shares have fallen in recent weeks in Santiago and New York as a result of concerns over the new tariffs, said brokers.
Electricity prices have been widely expected to fall sharply to reflect lower fuel costs as the result of the completion of a natural gas pipeline from Argentina next year.
